name: the_undivided
conceit: One composition holding two states of one subject (e.g., two goats at one moment of division); a code-only LEFT/RIGHT linear split-grade (not radial, unlike same_fire) gives each side its own visual fate; at the story's own turn the split resolves in code to one unified grade; a separate reference-chained plate (NOT an independently-guessed generation) receives the payoff the split plate was pointing toward.

anti: a correspondence-only story where two things simply need to be shown side-by-side without ever becoming one -- use the_double_entry_page or the_sounding_line instead
a geography or taxonomy story with no fate/state to split -- that is far_corner's or the_closed_file's job
a beat needing two independently-generated drawings to align -- the_registration_pull already proved that fails; the split here is 100% code on ONE plate, never two generations

plate_bill.must_contain: the veil/curtain of the sanctuary, woven work with cherubim, blue/purple/scarlet and fine linen texture (Exodus 26:31-33), not a plain modern drape
both goats present at once, ordinary domestic goats (not rams): one calm/still near the altar side, one already turning/oriented toward open ground (Leviticus 16:8-10, 16:21-22)
the Christ plate, passion register (Isaiah 53), gaunt and sorrowful bearing visible weight/burden, never idealized or heroic musculature, reference-chained off P2's palette/mood

motion_slots.earned_by: only the narration's own two motion beats -- the live goat actually being driven away, and the veil actually tearing top to bottom -- earn a paid Kling insert; the split-to-unified turn itself is a $0 code cross-dissolve, not a paid clip.

risk_flags: illustration_lock -- REQUIRED on all 3 plates, no 'photograph'/'museum'/'archival' language in any prompt
no_baked_text -- all KJV/verse text is Scribed Ink overlay applied post-render, never baked into a generation
accuracy_spec: Leviticus 16:8-10, 16:21-22 -- TWO male goats, one slain (blood brought within the veil), one live goat with the priest's hands laid on its head, confessed sins, sent away by the hand of a fit man; ordinary domestic goats, not rams (do not repeat this week's ram-for-lamb miss on a different animal).
Isaiah 53:6 (quoted KJV in the narration) -- 'the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all' -- the Christ plate must show the weight/burden being borne, not a triumphant or unmarked figure.
Exodus 26:31-33 -- the veil is a woven work with cherubim, blue/purple/scarlet/fine linen; avoid a plain modern drape.

beat_template.hook: the veil, an uncertain threshold, the law's two goats named
beat_template.pivot: one plate, both goats, split-graded into two fates -- then the split resolves to one unified grade at the story's own words 'no single creature could hold both halves'
beat_template.landing: the Christ plate, reference-chained off the goats, the fulfillment; the veil torn top to bottom, the substance named

caption_lane: lower-third, center -- clear of the veil's woven texture and the goats' heads in every plate
lettering: overlay_only -- the Isaiah 53:6 quote is the one verse card in the piece, Scribed Ink, timed to its own spoken window
score_shape: echo-shaped: one theme, cold/still under the goats' split state, warming through the unification cross-dissolve, full swell entering the Christ plate, sustained through the torn-veil beat, resolving to a quiet held CTA -- mirrors music_library's sacred_grace_rise arc, glory_holy_stillness as the landing pad.
